sim:1:User locks 1 BadToken for BSC, creating nonce 0xdeadbeef01; totalLocked[BadToken] increases, refunded[0xdeadbeef01] == false.
sim:2:Relay posts a faithful verified message to BSC, setting nonceUsed[0xdeadbeef01]=true and relayVerified[0xdeadbeef01]=true.
sim:3:Destination router mints 1 BadToken to attacker, marking mintedForNonce[0xdeadbeef01]=true.
sim:4:After timeout, attacker calls refund; require(!refunded[nonce]) passes (refunded == false), tokens are returned, and refunded[0xdeadbeef01] is set to true.

sim:2:Attacker‑controlled relay calls the router’s off‑chain verification entry. Due to a bug the router overwrites lockTimestamp[N] with the current block.timestamp instead of keeping the original value.

sim:4:Attacker triggers the mint on the destination chain using the same nonce. The bridge’s replay‑protection relies on the original lock timestamp; the overwritten (future) timestamp bypasses the check, allowing a second mint for the same lock.
